title: Air India Launches Non-Stop Delhi-Toronto Flights With New Boeing 787-9
excerpt: The airline will eliminate its Vienna fuel stop from August 1, cutting travel time by three hours and restoring daily service on one of its busiest North American routes.
body:
Air India announced on Wednesday that it will begin operating non-stop flights between Delhi and Toronto from August 1, deploying its factory-built Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on the route. The switch eliminates the airline's enroute fuel stop at Vienna, shaving roughly three hours off the westbound journey.

Under the new schedule, flight AI187 will depart Delhi at 1:45 a.m. and arrive in Toronto at 9:30 a.m. local time, with a flying time of about 17 hours — down from approximately 20 hours with the Vienna stop. The return service, flight AI188, will leave Toronto at 12:30 p.m. and reach Delhi at 2:05 p.m. the following day, with a non-stop flying time of up to 16 hours.

Air India will also restore daily frequencies on the route from August 1, up from the current five weekly flights. The airline had temporarily reduced service in June and July, citing unprecedented fuel price increases and broader geopolitical developments, according to The Tribune.

A New Cabin Product for a Key Corridor

The Delhi-Toronto route will be served by Air India's factory-built Boeing 787-9, featuring the airline's latest three-class configuration: 30 Business Class suites, 28 Premium Economy seats, and 238 Economy seats. The deployment marks the first time Air India's Premium Economy cabin will be available on the Toronto route.

Business Class passengers will get fully flat beds with direct aisle access, wireless charging, and 17-inch 4K entertainment screens. Premium Economy offers a 2-3-2 seating layout with 38-inch seat pitch. Across all cabins, passengers will have access to over 3,000 hours of content through the Thales AVANT Up system, Bluetooth audio connectivity, USB and AC power outlets, and redesigned amenity kits.

Air India's Transformation Gathers Speed

The Toronto upgrade is part of Air India's broader fleet modernization under its Vihaan.AI transformation program, launched after the Tata Group's acquisition of the carrier. The airline placed a landmark order for 470 aircraft from Boeing and Airbus, and has been progressively deploying new widebody jets across its long-haul network.

The first line-fit Boeing 787-9, custom-built for Air India, entered commercial service on the Mumbai-Frankfurt route in February 2026. CEO Campbell Wilson told media earlier this year that the airline expects to induct at least 20 widebody aircraft into long-haul operations during 2026, with a US$400 million investment underway to retrofit 25 additional Boeing 787 aircraft.

Wilson has previously highlighted Canada and North America as growth priorities. "We've added capacity into New York. We're increasing frequency in Toronto, and we're looking at potentially another couple of destinations in the reasonably near future in North America," he said at a media roundtable, according to Simple Flying.

What the Route Means for the Indian Diaspora in Canada

Canada is home to nearly 1.9 million people of Indian descent, according to the 2021 Census, making it the third-largest Indian diaspora community worldwide after the United States and the UAE. Over 812,000 Indian Canadians are concentrated in the Greater Toronto Area alone. India is also Canada's top source country for permanent residents, with more than 125,000 admitted in 2024.

The combination of restored daily frequencies and non-stop service is expected to improve connectivity for families, students, and professionals traveling between Delhi and the Toronto region.

What's Next

Bookings for the upgraded Delhi-Toronto service are now open through Air India's website, mobile app, customer contact centre, and travel agents. The airline is also in the process of retrofitting its legacy Boeing 787-8 fleet and 13 Boeing 777-300ER aircraft, with the full 787 retrofit program expected to be completed by 2027 — covering over 300 weekly flights to destinations across the United Kingdom, Europe, and Australia.
